qa.title: Q1456 (Aug. 8, 2025)
qa.question: When attacking using a follower with Twin Drive, if I reveal a Trigger with the first drive check, do I resolve the Trigger before or after performing the second drive check?
qa.answer: You resolve the Trigger first. qa.title: Q743 (Jun. 14, 2024)
qa.question: When my opponent has a Lyrial, Archer Throne with 5 or less defense on their field, why does playing Dance of Death not deal damage to the enemy leader, while playing Fiery Embrace with Spellchain (10) does?
qa.answer:
It has to do with the timing at which the enemy Lyrial is destroyed, or in other words, the duration for which its ability remains valid.

First, let's look at Dance of Death. When a follower's defense becomes 0 or less, it gets destroyed at the next Confirmation Timing, which occurs after the current ability—Dance of Death, in this case—is resolved. Therefore, when Dance of Death deals 2 damage to the enemy leader, Lyrial has 0 or less defense, but it's still on your opponent's field, so its ability is still valid, preventing its leader from taking ability damage.

Now let's look at Fiery Embrace with Spellchain (10). Effects indicated by an ability are applied in the written order, so the instruction "destroy it (the enemy follower)" is executed first, and Lyrial is immediately destroyed. By the time the instruction "deal 3 damage to that follower's leader" is executed, Lyrial is no longer on the field, so its ability isn't valid, and the enemy leader can take ability damage.

qa.title: Q742 (Jun. 14, 2024)
qa.question: If I deal 1 damage to my leader with an ability while this follower is on my field, my leader doesn't take any damage, but does Sanguine still become active for me? Does it count toward the number of times my leader has lost defense this turn?

qa.title: Q1047 (Jan. 31, 2025)
qa.question: I have 3 followers on my field, and I attack an enemy leader with this follower. If an opponent destroys one of my other followers with a Quick ability, do I still give this follower +1 attack with its Strike ability?
qa.answer:
Yes. During combat, your Strike abilities are resolved before opponents' Quick abilities; the active player's pending abilities are resolved before non-active players are able to respond.

In this case, even if a Quick ability would cause the number of followers on your field to drop below 3, this follower's Strike ability will have already been resolved.
